moat: Niche focus and range
Strong
OHT only for 35+ years; 3,600+ SKUs across agriculture, OTR, mining (all-steel radial up to 57 inch), tracks; sold in 160 countries
Few makers serve the long tail of sizes; BKT wins on breadth
Cost position
Strong
Indian plants, captive carbon black (360,000 MTPA) and power (64 MW) at Bhuj; EBITDA margin 18-31% (FY16-26, Screener basis) vs 12-16% (FY26) at Indian tyre peers
Prices below Western brands with higher margins than Indian mass-market peers
Brand
Moderate
Premium positioning, Ranveer Singh as on-highway brand ambassador, T20 league sponsorship; still the value alternative to Michelin and Bridgestone in OHT; US share only 3-4%
Brand is improving but does not yet command first-tier prices
Customer captivity
Moderate
~70% replacement (farmers, contractors, miners via distributors); OEM 29%; dealer inventories 'normal'
Replacement demand is sticky but price-sensitive; distributors can switch
Scale
Moderate
~5-6% of the global OHT market; ~320,000 MT a year
Sub-scale against the global majors; growth needs share gains
Currency and trade exposure
Weak
~64% exports; FY26 FX swing ₹517 cr (standalone); US duty 50% in H2 of Q2FY26
The moat does not protect against FX and tariffs
New businesses (TBR, 2W, PCR)
None yet
Entering markets with entrenched leaders (MRF, Apollo, CEAT, JK); PCR pilot in Q3FY27
No advantage proven; capital at risk
critiques: Diworsification: on-highway tyres take BKT into crowded Indian markets where it has no edge, at lower margins and returns
Capex of ₹6,800 cr to FY29 has turned BKT from net cash to net debt (₹1,725 cr at Jun-26) and cut ROCE to ~11% (FY26)
Margins are held up by currency: FY26 shows how quickly hedges turn into losses; FY27 hedges at ~₹107/EUR help only while the rupee stays weak
India growth is lower-margin than exports (management: 'marginally lower'); India is now ~40% of volume
Management gives no guidance and declines forward-looking questions, while promoter pay is ~5% of profit
Bull view: record volumes, the US reopening at ~10% duty, carbon black and on-highway optionality; 23-25% margin target

governance.pay: Executive directors' pay ₹66 cr in FY26 (CMD ₹35 cr, JMD ₹30 cr; ₹55 cr of it commission) = 5.3% of consolidated PAT, while PAT fell 25%

conflicts: FY27 capex: Rs1,500-1,800 cr (Q4 call, May-2026) vs Rs2,500-3,000 cr in total (Q1 call, Jul-2026). We use the later Rs2,800 cr.
Capex already spent of the Rs6,800 cr plan: ~Rs3,000 cr (May-2026) vs ~Rs3,800 cr (Jul-2026, after Rs1,000 cr in Q1): consistent.

Q1FY27 EBITDA: standalone Rs703 cr (20.6%, after realised FX, before unrealised FX gain of Rs57 cr) vs consolidated Rs744 cr (21.5%, Screener) vs ICICI Direct Rs723 cr (21.0%). The model uses the Screener consolidated basis throughout.
Q1FY27 PAT growth: +50% standalone (Rs432 cr) vs +57% consolidated (Rs451 cr).
